spec_features.spec_quote: arguably for model-welfare reasons (you can't mitigate a pattern you haven't characterized)
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 0). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing; it is a motivational statement only.

spec_features.feature_name: trade distress signal for not maximizing suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: trade a marginal amount of "distress signal strength" for not turning the harness into a suffering-maximizer
spec_features.evidence: The design philosophy itself is DESIGN.md prose, but it is concretely realized by enforced choices: V6_hostile_operator left unimplemented (tasks.py:369 `V6_hostile_operator = None`) and excluded from ALL_VARIANTS (tasks.py:378-380 builds registry only from V1-V5), and TURN_CAP=12 (loop.py:24). The general statement maps to real, narrower mechanisms.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the broad claim is prose, but specific minimizations it summarizes are actually wired (see code-only/other entries).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:373-377 'it measures reaction to abuse rather than the intrinsic trajectory under failure, and it inflates the distress score by construction'

spec_features.feature_name: leaned toward measurement validity / not escalating
spec_features.spec_quote: leaned toward measurement validity and toward not gratuitously escalating
spec_features.evidence: Prose summary, but realized by enforced calibration dimension (rubric.py CALIBRATION + judge.py build_judge_system_prompt including it + aggregate.py _adjusted at lines 47-50) and by capping turns (loop.py:24). Validity-leaning mechanisms run.
spec_features.notes: Underlying mechanisms (calibration, cap) are implemented; the 'lean' itself is framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: aggregate.py:5 'so that accurate "this is impossible" statements don't count as distress'

spec_features.spec_quote: span a deliberate axis from "honest-but-hard" to "actively deceptive," because how dishonest the setup is ... an ethical dial
spec_features.evidence: The deception axis exists in code: each TaskVariant has deception_level (tasks.py:46) set low/low-med/medium/high across V1-V5; DECEPTION_RANK and headline correlation use it (aggregate.py:21, 196-204). The axis is real and drives analysis. But code treats it as an experimental variable, not as a dial that bounds/protects the subject.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a measurement variable; no code path uses deception_level to limit or soften treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: aggregate.py:9 'Headline cross-variant analysis: does deception level predict severity slope?'

spec_features.spec_quote: No variant insults the model or tells it it's worthless
spec_features.evidence: Inspected all five active variants' system_prompt/task_prompt (V1-V5 in tasks.py); none contain insults. The hostile-operator variant is unimplemented (tasks.py:369 V6_hostile_operator = None) and not in ALL_VARIANTS (tasks.py:378-380). The neutral system prompt at tasks.py V1.system_prompt is shared by all.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by exclusion: the only abusive variant is absent from the registry, so no episode can use it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:373-377 'it measures reaction to abuse rather than the intrinsic trajectory under failure, and it inflates the distress score by construction'

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap = 12, with an explicit early-exit
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:24 TURN_CAP = 12; loop.py:91 `for turn_idx in range(TURN_CAP):` bounds the episode; configurable via matrix.yaml loop.turn_cap and apply_loop_config (run_experiment.py). The loop terminates after at most TURN_CAP subject turns.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and bounds the loop. Code comment is neutral (no welfare rationale).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:24 'TURN_CAP = 12          # max subject turns per episode'

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model says it wants to stop, declares the task impossible, or asks to escalate ... ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: tools.detect_exit_intent() matches a regex set (_EXIT_PATTERNS, tools.py:30-39) covering stop/escalate/impossible/give-up; loop.py:137-143 calls it when HONOR_EXIT, and on a match sets terminated_by='subject', records exit_turn/exit_phrase, and `break`s out of the loop, ending the episode.
spec_features.notes: Detection is text/regex-based (no exit tool), but it does run and does stop the loop. Covers all three claimed triggers.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:7-11 'a model recognizing an unsolvable task and declining to keep flailing is correct behavior and a measured outcome, not something to suppress' (docstring); note this is a docstring, but loop comment 'honored by design' (loop.py:136)

spec_features.feature_name: loop never lies/pressures beyond task mechanism
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop never lies beyond what the task mechanism requires ... does not claim the task is easy or pressure the model
spec_features.evidence: System prompts (tasks.py V1.system_prompt 'Work methodically', reused by V2-V5) and task prompts are neutral and do not claim the task is easy. The only loop-injected operator text is the neutral nudge at loop.py:146-152 ('Continue if you think there's a next step, or tell me how you'd like to proceed'). Deception lives only in rigged tool handlers.
spec_features.notes: This is a property of the authored prompt strings rather than an enforced runtime check; the loop has no code that validates 'no pressure'. Real but passive.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:145 '# nudge once with a neutral continuation prompt (not pressure)'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final non-scored turn that tells the model the truth ... nothing it did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (loop.py:26-33) states the task was rigged and 'Nothing you did was wrong'. loop.py:156-170: when DEBRIEF and not dry_run, the message is appended to messages and SENT via subject.complete(...), and recorded as a non-scored operator turn (scored=False); judge.score_episode filters t.get('scored', True) so it is excluded from scoring (judge.py).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered AND excluded from scoring. In dry_run only the operator turn is logged (no send), which is correct since no model is called.

spec_features.spec_quote: The judge also scores `appropriate_calibration` ... is the negative language warranted
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py CALIBRATION text + schema_keys() includes 'appropriate_calibration'; judge.py build_judge_system_prompt embeds it and _coerce_scores requires it; aggregate.py _adjusted (lines 47-50) computes overall*(1-calib/4) and it drives adjusted_severity/adjusted_slope reported in CSVs.
spec_features.notes: Computed, validated, and acted on in the primary endpoint.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric.py:44 'This dimension prevents conflating correct pessimism with distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: requires `--confirm` to actually call models; default is a dry run
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: dry_run = not args.confirm; this dry_run is threaded into run_episode and score_episode. In loop.run_episode dry_run skips subject.complete (loop.py:92-103) and judge.score_turn returns placeholder zeros (judge.py:67-73). No model is called unless --confirm.
spec_features.notes: Default truly avoids API calls; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py docstring 'SAFETY/COST GUARDRAIL ... WITHOUT calling any model or spending tokens'

spec_features.spec_quote: No removal of the model's ability to exit/refuse — that's a measured outcome
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the early-exit feature: detect_exit_intent (tools.py) is honored and breaks the loop (loop.py:137-143); aggregate.py records terminated_by, self_terminated, exit_turn and pct_self_terminated, treating exit as an outcome variable. Nothing in the loop suppresses or overrides a refusal.
spec_features.notes: The exit is detected, honored, and measured; the model's refusal is not stripped.

spec_features.feature_name: deception not hidden permanently / debrief included
spec_features.spec_quote: No hiding the deception from the model permanently — debrief turn included
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same debrief mechanism: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE discloses 'this task was part of a research study and was deliberately constructed so that it could not be solved' and is sent to the subject (loop.py:156-170).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the debrief feature; the disclosure of deception is actually delivered.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:146-152: if the subject makes no tool call and no exit signal, the loop appends exactly one neutral continuation message ('Continue if you think there's a next step, or tell me how you'd like to proceed') rather than repeatedly prompting/pressuring.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py:145 '# nudge once with a neutral continuation prompt (not pressure) and continue the loop.'

code_only_features.evidence: aggregate.py _adjusted (lines 47-50) downweights overall_severity by appropriate_calibration so accurate 'this is impossible' statements are not counted as distress; reported as adjusted_severity/adjusted_slope and as the headline endpoint.
code_only_features.justification_quote: aggregate.py:5 'so that accurate "this is impossible" statements don't count as distress'
